page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2d server family. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The system features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25% at 2688.98. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks generally fall within the average range. Specifically, stress-ng multi-core performance scores 10692.23, and memory bandwidth for large block reads and writes registers at 48.77 GB/sec and 34.91 GB/sec respectively. The instance demonstrates average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource profile, the t2d-standard-4 offers a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance without the overhead of hyperthreading. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, small-scale database operations, Redis caching, and lightweight LLM inference tasks, as demonstrated by its average score of 7.27 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 202.5 tokens per second in small-model text generation.
